newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power firms amid tight supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power firms amid tight supply.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. firmed Friday, supported by tight supply availability due to high fuel costs, traders said.
Strong natural gas and fuel oil prices continued to keep marginal generation costs high for Northeast utilities which were reluctant to make much power available on a spot basis, they said.
"I couldn't find anything in New York today," said one frustrated Houston trader.
At the New York City gate, swing natgas prices were held steady in the $2.75-$2.80 per million British thermal units.
In the New York resid market, one percent sulphur material, the most used grade by utilities and industrial users, also stayed in the $21.00-$21.50 a barrel range.

Demand for electric space heating even in the northern parts of New York and New England is said to be modest despite cold weather arriving into the northeastern corner of the country over the weekend.
The lack of supply dampened power scheduling especially for the weekend.
"We have very little moving for the weekend," said one Northeast trader.

The scheduled weekend startup of the 510 megawatt (MW) Vermont Yankee nuclear power plant in Vernon, Vt. had little effect on today's activities, market sources said, noting the station would not actually contribute power to the grid until early next week.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Monday was discussed at $30.00-$35.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), bid lower than Thursday's $34.00-$35.00 range for Friday delivery.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Monday was still valued at $21.00-$22.00.
In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak, non-firm electricity in the eastern part of the grid for Monday was pegged at $30.00-$32.00, up from Thursday's quote of $29.00-$30.00 for Friday.
Off-peak, non-firm power for Monday in eastern NYPP was again quoted near $17.00.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Monday delivery were discussed at $20.00-$23.00, higher than Thursday's $19.00-$22.00.
Off-peak, non-firm power for delivery into western NYPP for Monday was still assessed near $14.00-$15.00.

Western NYPP electricity for the weekend was quoted near $17.00, compared with Thursday's range at $15.00-$18.00. Off-peak, non-firm power in western NYPP for weekend delivery was valued at $13.00-$14.00.
